_source: NED (NASA/IPAC Extragalactic Database), Tully et al. 2014, McConnachie 2012
_note: Distances in Mly (million light-years) from Milky Way. Positions are approximate.

major_galaxies.name: Andromeda
major_galaxies.note: Will collide with Milky Way in ~4.5 Gyr.

major_galaxies.name: Triangulum
major_galaxies.note: Third-largest Local Group galaxy. Barely visible to naked eye.

major_galaxies.name: Large Magellanic Cloud
major_galaxies.note: Largest Milky Way satellite. Visible from Southern Hemisphere.

major_galaxies.name: Small Magellanic Cloud
major_galaxies.note: Connected to LMC by Magellanic Stream of gas.

named_structures.name: Virgo Cluster
named_structures.note: Core of Virgo Supercluster. Richest cluster within 100 Mly.

named_structures.name: Great Attractor
named_structures.note: Obscured by galactic plane (Zone of Avoidance). Known only from velocity flows.

named_structures.name: Centaurus A
named_structures.note: Nearest radio galaxy; active AGN with relativistic jets.

nearby_superclusters.name: Shapley Concentration
nearby_superclusters.note: Largest known mass concentration within ~1 Gly. ~8,000 galaxies.

nearby_superclusters.name: Coma Supercluster
nearby_superclusters.note: Rich supercluster; one of first clusters where dark matter was inferred (Zwicky 1933).

nearby_superclusters.name: Perseus-Pisces Filament
nearby_superclusters.note: Major filamentary structure; Perseus cluster (Abell 426) at core.

voids.name: Boötes Void
voids.note: One of the largest known voids. Expected ~2,000 galaxies if uniformly distributed; only ~60 found.

voids.name: Eridanus Void
voids.note: Large void in southern sky. May be related to the CMB Cold Spot.

voids.name: Sculptor Void
voids.note: Southern void adjacent to Pisces-Cetus supercomplex.
